sites.functional_impact_measured: Ouabain-resistance assay: alpha1 subunit with HA tag at pos 119 conferred ouabain resistance (function preserved). Surface immunofluorescence of intact cells: tag detected extracellularly (surface expression confirmed). Evidence is from alpha1 paralog; direct functional data for alpha3 at this position NOT MEASURED.
sites.rationale: [Literature audit 2026-11-05 (deliverome-analysis PR 236), verdict region_only: insert_after_residue 109 -> NULL; the paper names a region, not a junction (region: ECL1 (paralog site: rat ATP1A1 A119 maps to ATP1A3 ~A109; no ATP1A3 construct)). validation_level surface_and_function -> detected_only (paper reports surface: not_reported, function: not_reported). Paper (PMID 8916902): "double tags at positions 119 and 318 were located extracellularly". Audit note: Paper tagged rat alpha1 only; no ATP1A3 construct exists. Alignment does map alpha1 A119 to alpha3 A109 (alpha3 lacks 10 N-terminal residues), but the rationale's claim that ECL1 is identical is false (alpha1 AYSIQAATEEEPQNDN vs alpha3 AYGIQAGTEDDPSGDN). Paralog-derived, so surface/function are not shown for ATP1A3.] L2 (PMID 8916902) explicitly confirms by intact-cell immunofluorescence that the HA tag at alpha1 position 119 is extracellular, and L1 confirms ouabain resistance (functional pump). Alpha1 and alpha3 ECL1 carry the identical sequence 'LAYGIQAGTEDDPSGDNLY'; alpha1 has 10 extra N-terminal residues, so alpha1 pos 119 (7th residue of ECL1) maps to alpha3 pos 109 by sequence alignment. Alpha3 pos 109 lies in ECL1 (103-121), 7 residues from TM1 end (102) and 13 residues from TM2 start (122), satisfying the >=3-residue constraint on both sides. Evidence is indirect (alpha1 paralog). PMID 8916902 inserted a double HA epitope tag at position 119 of the full-length membrane-anchored alpha1 Na+/K+-ATPase subunit (ATP1A1, 1023 aa) expressed in transfected cells. Immunofluorescence of intact (non-permeabilized) cells confirmed the tag at alpha1 pos 119 is extracellular. Alpha1 and alpha3 share ~87% identity; alpha1 has 10 additional N-terminal cytoplasmic residues. The ECL1 sequence 'LAYGIQAGTEDDPSGDNLY' is identical in both isoforms. Alpha1 pos 119 is the 7th residue of ECL1 (alpha1 ECL1 starts at ~113); the equivalent 7th residue in alpha3 ECL1 (103-121) is pos 109 (A). Python-verified: seq[108]='A', seq[109]='G'.
sites.residue_label: ECL1 (paralog site: rat ATP1A1 A119 maps to ATP1A3 ~A109; no ATP1A3 construct)

sources.claim: Immunofluorescence analysis of permeabilized and intact cells using a monoclonal antibody specific for the HA epitope showed that double tags at positions 119 and 318 were located extracellularly, whereas single or double tags at positions 173, 815, 881, 987, and 1023 were cytoplasmically disposed. These results are consistent with an eight transmembrane domain arrangement for the alpha subunit.
sources.title: Localization of cytoplasmic and extracellular domains of Na,K-ATPase by epitope tag insertion

sites.functional_impact_measured: Ouabain-resistance assay: alpha1 subunit with HA tag at pos 318 conferred ouabain resistance (function preserved). Surface immunofluorescence of intact cells: tag detected extracellularly. Evidence is from alpha1 paralog; direct data for alpha3 ECL2 NOT MEASURED.
sites.rationale: [Literature audit 2026-11-05 (deliverome-analysis PR 236), verdict region_only: region-level site confirmed; no junction recoverable. validation_level surface_and_function -> detected_only (paper reports surface: not_reported, function: not_reported). Paper (PMID 8916902): "An antigenic peptide derived from the hemagglutinin (HA) of influenza virus was inserted at 15 different positions within the rat Na,K-ATPase alpha 1 subunit isoform. ... Immunofluorescence analysis of permeabilized and intact cells using a monoclonal antibody specific for the HA epitope showed that double tags at positions 119 and 318 were located extracellularly". Audit note: Abstract only (pubs.acs.org serves a bot check in both browsers; no PMC), as for the ATP1A1-119/318 training rows. The paper tags rat alpha1 (ATP1A1) only; no ATP1A3 construct exists, so this is paralog-derived evidence, consistent with the region_only verdict on ATP1A3-109. The only exact junction, rat alpha1 318 (L318|E319 in the 7-residue TM3-TM4 loop), maps by alignment to human alpha3 P13637 L308|E309 (FILSLILGYTWL|EAVIFLIGIIVA, -10 offset), the position the row's own rationale rejected as 2 residues from TM4; recorded here only for reference, not as a corrected residue.] L2 (PMID 8916902) confirms by intact-cell immunofluorescence that the HA tag at alpha1 pos 318 is extracellular, and L1 confirms ouabain resistance. Alpha1 pos 318 is the 10th residue of ECL2 (alpha1 ECL2 ~309-319 in alpha1 numbering); the sequence-equivalent position in alpha3 ECL2 (299-309) is pos 308, which is only 2 residues from TM4 (310) and fails the >=3-residue constraint. Because no specific alpha3 residue within ECL2 can be pinned from the published alpha1 position without violating the constraint, the site is reported at region level (ECL2, null residue). Evidence is indirect (alpha1 paralog). PMID 8916902 inserted a double HA epitope tag at position 318 of the full-length membrane-anchored alpha1 Na+/K+-ATPase subunit (ATP1A1, 1023 aa). Intact-cell immunofluorescence (L2) confirmed the tag at alpha1 pos 318 is extracellular. Alpha1 pos 318 maps to the 10th residue of ECL2 (alpha1 ECL2 ~309-319); the equivalent in alpha3 ECL2 (299-309) is pos 308, which is only 2 residues from TM4 start (310) and fails the >=3-residue constraint. No alpha3 residue within ECL2 satisfying the constraint can be pinned to the published alpha1 pos 318; the site is therefore reported at region level.
